1: Hear, son of Pṛthā, how you will know me in full and without doubt, with your mind attached to me, practising yoga and taking me as your refuge.
2: I will tell you this knowledge, together with discernment, leaving nothing out. Once you know it, nothing further remains here to be known.
3: Among thousands of people, perhaps one strives for perfection. And even among those who strive and are perfected, perhaps one knows me as I truly am.
4: Earth, water, fire, air, space, mind, buddhi too, and the sense of I: this is my nature, divided in eight.
5: This is the lower nature. But know my other nature, mighty-armed one, which is higher than this. It has become the living being, and by it this world is held up.
6: Understand that all beings have this as their womb. I am the origin of the whole world, and its dissolution as well.
7: There is nothing else at all higher than me, winner of wealth. All this is strung on me, like clusters of gems on a thread.
8: I am the taste in water, son of Kuntī. I am the light of the moon and the sun, the syllable Om in all the Vedas, the sound in space and the manhood in men.
9: And I am the pure fragrance in the earth and the brilliance in fire. I am the life in all beings, and I am the austerity in ascetics.
10: Know me, son of Pṛthā, as the eternal seed of all beings. I am the buddhi of the intelligent. I am the brilliance of the brilliant.
11: And I am the strength of the strong, a strength free from desire and passion. In beings, bull of the Bharatas, I am the desire that does not go against dharma.
12: And whatever states of being come from sattva, and whatever come from rajas and from tamas, know that they are from me alone. But I am not in them. They are in me.
13: Deluded by these three states of being, made of the guṇas, this whole world does not recognise me, who am higher than these and imperishable.
14: For this divine illusion of mine, made of the guṇas, is hard to cross. Those who take refuge in me alone cross over this illusion.
15: The evildoers, the deluded, the lowest of men, do not take refuge in me. Illusion has carried away their knowledge, and they have taken to the demonic state of being.
16: Four kinds of people who do good worship me, Arjuna: the one in distress, the one who wishes to know, the one who seeks gain, and the one who knows, bull of the Bharatas.
17: Of these, the one who knows stands out, always yoked and devoted to one. For I am exceedingly dear to the one who knows, and that one is dear to me.
18: All of these are noble indeed, but the one who knows is the very self: that is my view. For such a one, with the self yoked, has turned to me alone as the unsurpassed goal.
19: At the end of many births, the one who has knowledge takes refuge in me, knowing that Vāsudeva is all. Such a great self is very hard to find.
20: Those whose knowledge has been carried away by one desire or another take refuge in other gods. They take up one observance or another, constrained by their own nature.
21: Whatever form any devotee wishes to worship with faith, I make that very faith of theirs unshakable.
22: Joined with that faith, the devotee seeks to worship that form, and from it obtains what is desired. For those desires are granted by me alone.
23: But the fruit those of little understanding gain has an end. Those who sacrifice to the gods go to the gods. My devotees, in turn, come to me.
24: Those without buddhi think of me, the unmanifest, as something that has come into manifestation. They do not know my higher state of being, imperishable and unsurpassed.
25: I am not visible to all, covered as I am by the illusion of yoga. This deluded world does not recognise me, the unborn, the imperishable.
26: I know the beings that have passed, Arjuna, those that are present and those that are to come. But no one at all knows me.
27: Through the delusion of the pairs of opposites, which arises from wanting and aversion, descendant of Bharata, all beings fall into delusion at birth, scorcher of foes.
28: But people of pure action, whose evil has come to an end, are freed from the delusion of the pairs of opposites. They worship me, firm in their vows.
29: Those who take refuge in me and strive for release from old age and death know that brahman, the whole of what concerns the self, and action in its entirety.
30: Those who know me together with what concerns beings and what concerns the gods, and together with what concerns sacrifice, have minds that are yoked. They know me even at the time of departure.
